newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures begin lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures begin lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures opened lower in moderate trade, hampered by profit-taking worries.
On Monday, September Standard and Poor's 500 futures wiped out early gains and ended slightly lower, leaving some traders to worry about weakness again today.
"Yesterday it was evident to me that regardless of the bond rallies we couldn't get anything going," one S&P 500 futures trader said. "I think the risk is for profit-taking today," he added.
September slipped to a 937.80 session low early.
One firm pegged September S&P 500 fair value at 5.00 points premium to cash, buy programs at 6.30 points premium to cash or wider and sells at 4.70 points premium or narrower.

Traders noted scant followthrough into stock index futures pits from early data. Second-quarter U.S. employment cost index (ECI) was reported as expected, up 0.8 percent from an 0.6 percent gain in the first quarter. BTM/Schroders reported chain store sales up 0.4 percent in the week ended July 26.
September S&Ps very briefly cut losses after July U.S. consumer confidence was reported at 126.5 versus a revised 129.9 in June.
Traders were awaiting second-quarter gross domestic product on Thursday and July jobs data on Friday.
A Reuters poll of economists showed an average forecast of July jobs up 193,000, versus a 217,000 June gain. The jobless rate was seen at 4.9 percent, down from 5.0 percent in June.
At 0907 CDT/1407 GMT, Sept S&P 500s were down 3.45 pts to 940.20, Nikkei fell 240.0 pts to 20,410.0, Midcap 400s fell 0.35 to 308.70, Russell fell 0.10 to 411.00, and NASDAQ rose 1.75 to 1085.00.
